page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a virtual machine within the High Frequency Compute family, built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel processor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 384 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the average category, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and physical core limitations. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 497.33 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak, dropping to 35.47 GB/sec and 17.49 GB/sec respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the vhf-4c-16gb is its shared CPU model and weak performance in high-throughput tasks. It exhibits weak results in static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression. Consequently, this server is less suited for heavy database deployments or high-traffic web hosting. It is best utilized for general-purpose workloads, development environments, lightweight background workers, or Redis caching where strong single-core bursts are beneficial but sustained multi-core saturation is not required.
